title: outboxSyncWriteFacadeProvider mutates DAO state and fires a network re-enqueue from inside its Provider build function
why: The code directly inside `Provider<OutboxSyncWriteFacade?>((ref) {...})` mutates pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and unawaited-fires reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows(profileId) unconditionally on every build. This provider watches authStateProvider, activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider, userDatabaseProvider, activeProfileIdProvider, and localDayClockProvider -- any of which changing (e.g. every profile switch in this multi-child app) reruns build and refires the recovery scan, which its own D14 comment says is meant to run once. SM-2 exists precisely because 'side effects in build race and get skipped or duplicated on rebuild' -- here they duplicate on every rebuild instead of running once.
recommendation: Move syncSink wiring and the one-time ledger-recovery call out of build into a ref.listen/onDispose pairing or an explicit one-shot recovery triggered on cloud-conversion, leaving build to only construct and return the facade.
acceptance_criteria: riverpod_lint/custom_lint rule flagging DAO field mutation or unawaited async calls directly inside a Provider build body (SM-2 Enforce backstop).
Regression test with a spy DAO asserting reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows is invoked at most once per profile per session, not once per rebuild (simulate two profile switches).

corrections: The finding's 'why' misquotes sync_providers.dart:175's own comment (actual text: 'Idempotent + fire-and-forget so it never blocks the UI', not 'meant to run once'). points_balance_dao.dart:559-567's doc comment on reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows explicitly states it is idempotent and should be 'call[ed] right after wiring syncSink (cloud session start / profile switch)' — refiring on every profile switch is the designed behavior, not the duplication bug SM-2 warns about. The bare side-effect-in-build pattern smell is still real, but there is no demonstrated concrete cost, so this is hygiene not design debt.
